messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: PROD alert: p99 latency for inference-router spiked to ~2200ms in us-west-2, p95 ~480ms. Streaming stall rate +18%. Paging oncall.
oncall-rohit: I'm on it. Pulling dashboards now — seeing tail blowup aligned with router LB traffic skew and rising backend queue depth.
sre-ellie: joining tty. Can you dump routing table heatmap? I want to see shard distribution.
infra-james: pulling router metrics -> note a config change at 02:03 UTC: routing-policy v3 rollout (prefer-local bump) went live. I pushed a small weight tweak.
eng-maya: that rollout was supposed to be gradual. Did the feature flag flip?
infra-james: flag was incremental but one seed host applied full weight accidentally (human operator error).
oncall-rohit: hypothesis: v3 policy caused hot partitioning -> lots of requests hitting same router shards -> kv cache miss + backend queueing -> tail latency. Plan: 1) pin traffic back to policy v2 2) scale router-pool 3) enable eager fallback to compatible model. Rolling step 1 now.
ops-qa: FYI support sees partial transcript timeouts from streaming sessions. Customers impacted: two enterprise accounts timing out. Support notified.
eng-maya: rollback command (control-plane):
```
curl -X POST https://control.redwood/api/v1/policies/rollback \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN_TOKEN" \
  -d '{"policy":"routing-policy","version":"v2"}'
```
infra-james: executing rollback...
incident-bot: control-plane: rollback request accepted (req_id: rp-92f3).
infra-james: rollback completed on seed hosts, propagating.
sre-ellie: watching p99 and streaming stall metric. Also checking LB logs for misroutes -> seeing many cross-zone handoffs to eu-west when us-west capacity is congested. That adds ~200-500ms per request.
ml-ana: KV cache hit ratio on hot keys dropped from 84% -> 22% during skew, explains extra backend cost.
oncall-rohit: p99 dropping to ~920ms post-rollback, p95 260ms. Still above ideal but improving.
sre-ellie: I'm going to scale router-pool by +30% to relieve queued requests. Doing ASG bump.
ops-qa: scaling started. Also I applied a temporary routing weight cap so no single seed gets >8% of traffic.
support-lin: support update: customers A and B confirmed degraded transcripts; both have been given incident notice and workaround (switch to shorter session window). Ops: please capture logs for RM request ids.
infra-james: ASG bump done, pods in service. Observing fewer cross-zone handoffs.
oncall-rohit: p99 steadying ~700ms now, streaming stall rate down to +3% vs baseline.
sre-ellie: good. Root cause looks like two-fold: 1) rollout flag misapply created a hot seed weight; 2) routing-policy v3 logic amplified hotkey fanout (binning behavior) for long-tail keys. We'll need a fix for the policy logic.
ml-ana: recommendation: add per-key smoothing and a hotkey cap in policy v3 + pre-warming KV cache on handoff. Add a metric for bin imbalance.
eng-maya: agree. Will create a PR with unit tests for smoothing and a canary gate for weight limits.
oncall-rohit: handing off to ellie for post-mitigation triage and postmortem. I'm going to sleep on-call but reachable.
sre-ellie: taking over. I'll keep the bridge open for another 20m to watch. Next steps: 1) postmortem w/ timeline and RCA, 2) rollback guard (automated check on seed weight), 3) add canary + gradual rollout enforcement, 4) update runbook for streaming customer communications.
ops-qa: logging snapshot saved -> s3://incidents/6472600000/snapshot.log.cc.
support-lin: I'll follow up with affected customers and share timeline once PM draft is ready.
incident-bot: Status changed to RESOLVED (after manual verify).
oncall-rohit: TL;DR: latency spike caused by routing-policy v3 rollout accidentally applied at high weight to a seed host, producing hot partitioning and cross-zone misroutes. Immediate rollback + pool scaling mitigated. Postmortem owners: eng-maya (policy fix), infra-james (rollback guard), ml-ana (cache prewarm & metrics), sre-ellie (postmortem doc).
sre-ellie: filing postmortem now and will schedule follow-up review. Closing thread in 1 hour unless other issues. :white_check_mark:
